The quarter-hyperbola above is defined by the parametric equations

$$
x=\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=2\operatorname{sec}⁡t.
$$

Determine the domain of the parameter $t$ for this quarter, assuming that the entire hyperbola is defined only for $t\in [-\pi ,\pi ].$

$t\in (${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$]$
worked_solution:
The parametric equations of the full hyperbola are

$$
x=\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=2\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,t\in [-\pi ,\pi ],\,t\ne \pm \frac{\pi }{2}.
$$

To restrict the parameterization to a quarter-hyperbola, we refer to the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14093765/assets/cf47cf9e617f29a25ddd353448d8df1855ccf778b2f5ce304d534161f683cf16.png)

We can see that if we restrict $t$ to $(-\frac{\pi }{2},0]$ we get the required quarter-hyperbola.

Therefore, the parametric equations that describe the required quarter-hyperbola are

$$
x=\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=2\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,t\in (-\frac{\pi }{2},0].
$$
